pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - Stanley Park Infants' School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Headteacher’s Welcome
At Stanley Park Infants’ School, we are proud to be a welcoming and inclusive community with a strong reputation for excellence in teaching and learning.
Our committed and talented team deliver an ambitious structured curriculum, with high expectations for all. Our curriculum is enriched through a wide range of purposeful learning experiences, including lessons, visits and extra-curricular opportunities.
We provide a nurturing, caring and supportive environment where pupils feel safe, valued and ready to learn. Our strong culture of inclusion ensures that all children are supported to thrive academically and personally.
Our Parent Teacher Friends Association plays an important role in strengthening our school community through fundraising and social events.
Our governors provide effective support and challenge, playing an active role in the strategic leadership of the school.
Stanley Park Infants’ School is a very special place to learn, work and grow where relationships are at the heart of everything we do.
We warmly welcome visits to the school and encourage you to arrange an appointment to meet our staff and children by contacting the school office.
I look forward to meeting you.
David D’Souza Headteacher
'Stanley Park Infants’ is a school that truly cares for both the pupils and families they serve. For many staff it is evident that this is more than a job, it is a vocation.
It was a pleasure to work with a team so passionate and committed to ensuring the best outcomes for the children in their community.' Safeguarding Review 2025

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Vision and Values - Stanley Park Infants' School
pageCache.text:
Our Vision and Values
At Stanley Park Infants School, we are a forward-thinking and inclusive learning community where every child is valued, safe and inspired to succeed.
We are committed to providing a high-quality, ambitious and well-sequenced curriculum that equips pupils with the essential knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to thrive. We maintain consistently high expectations, ensuring that all pupils, regardless of their starting points or individual needs, achieve their full potential.
Our school fosters a culture of curiosity, resilience and excellence, where children are encouraged to take risks, ask thoughtful questions and embrace challenge. Through a carefully designed environment, pupils develop confidence, independence and a strong sense of responsibility for their learning.
We place children’s well-being, safety and personal development at the heart of everything we do, creating a nurturing and respectful environment where every child feels happy, secure and ready to learn, and where safeguarding is everyone’s responsibility.
We are proud of our inclusive ethos, working closely with families and the wider community to remove barriers to learning and ensure every child belongs and succeeds. We promote positive relationships, mutual respect and understanding, enabling children to become kind, respectful and active members of society.
Through strong leadership, reflective practice and a commitment to continuous improvement, we strive for excellence in all aspects of school life, ensuring every child leaves Stanley Park Infants School well-prepared for the next stage of their education and for life beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - Stanley Park Infants' School
pageCache.text:
British Values
The Department for Education states that there is a need for schools to promote fundamental British values. These are:
At Stanley Park Infants’ School we are continually enriching and developing our curriculum so that it incorporates British values as part of our daily practice.
We actively reinforce these values in a wide variety of ways:
Pupils learn what is right and wrong through classroom charters, school rules, our Busy Bee code and also through the Behaviour Policy.
We hold an anti-bullying week each year and do regular work on this through PSHE and assemblies.
On Monday’s Mrs Smith meets with all the year groups in Hive Assembly where she celebrates good choices, here we discuss our pupil choices, Busy Bee Code and think about ways to regulate our emotions, resulting in more positive behaviour.
Positions on the School Council and the Eco star Team are decided through a democratic process involving all pupils. Our School Council meet regularly to discuss important decisions, share the voice of the children and support Mr D’ Souza in leading the school.
Tolerance of difference
We celebrate difference at Stanley Park Infants’ School, we recognise that we all come from different backgrounds and have unique lived experiences. We respect these and ensure home languages and cultures are represented in our school environment. Throughout the year we teach about different cultures, customs and celebrations and also enjoy many immersion events where children experience food, music and learn about languages.
All incidents of racism and bullying related to protected characteristics (i.e. age, disability, gender reassignment, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, marriage and civil partnership, and pregnancy and maternity) are registered on our reporting system
The school issues weekly rewards for politeness and considerate behaviour. Our Pupil Choices are our basis for all modelling positive behaviours and mutual respect for all.
All staff consistently model mutual respect in their dealings with children and parents/carers.
All pupils are made aware of their individual responsibility in making choices and decisions. We support pupils in their understanding of the world around them to help them make informed choices about their health and well-being.
Our behaviour policy (available on the Policies Page) embeds the idea of consequences based on choice and action. Our reflective process ensures pupils have the opportunity to unpick their behaviours and look at how it has affected both themselves and others.

PE and Sport Premium
At Stanley Park Infants' School, children benefit hugely from the PE and Sport Premium Funding for Primary Schools. We aim to develop and improve our PE curriculum and sporting opportunities through the use of funding, as well as ensuring that the improvements made are maintained and sustainable for pupils in years to come.
The funding can be used in a variety of ways to provide children with fantastic opportunities before, during and after the school day to encourage them to live healthy, active lifestyles. The following sports funding report explains the break down of costs, impact and sustainability of the funding. The funding aims to improve sport and Physical Education through five key indicators:

pageCache.pageTitle: Prospective Parent Information - Stanley Park Infants' School
pageCache.text:
Prospective Parent Information
Welcome
Welcome to our school, where every child is valued, supported and encouraged to Be the Best They Can Be. Guided by our Busy Bee Code, we nurture a warm, caring and inclusive environment where children from all backgrounds feel safe, confident and ready to learn. We celebrate diversity, promote respect and inspire curiosity, enabling every child to grow, flourish and succeed both academically and socially.
Open Mornings for Entry September 2027
Open mornings for entry September 2027 will be held on the following dates from 9.30am - 10.30am; please click on the dates to book your place.
Tuesday 13th October 2026
Tuesday 3rd November 2026
Wednesday 4th November 2026
Tuesday 12th January 2027
Open Door Policy
We are proud of our open-door policy and the strong relationships we build with our families. We warmly welcome visits to our school, so please feel free to contact us to arrange an appointment and experience our wonderful learning environment. Parents and carers are always welcome to speak with staff before and after the school day. Together, we create a caring, supportive community where every child feels valued and is encouraged to thrive.
Inclusion and SEND
Inclusion is at the heart of our school, where every child is valued, respected and supported to thrive. We celebrate individuality and ensure all children feel a true sense of belonging in everything we do.
Please click the link below for more information.
Lunch
Our lunches are freshly prepared on site and offer a varied, nutritious menu designed to suit all tastes and dietary needs. Options include vegetarian and halal choices, as well as jacket potatoes, hot meals and a fresh salad bar. We are committed to ensuring every child enjoys a balanced diet that supports their learning and wellbeing, with a fruit-based dessert available each day and a special treat to look forward to on Fridays.
Parents can conveniently select their child’s meal choices each day using Arbor.
Wrap Around Care
We offer a wide range of flexible wrap-around care to support busy families. Our school-led Breakfast Club, Busy Bees, and after-school club, Bumbles, provide a warm, familiar environment led by staff who know the children well, ensuring activities are tailored to their individual needs. Children enjoy games, outdoor play and a relaxed, picnic-style tea in a fun and supportive setting.
We also work in partnership with Jancett Playsafe, who are based on site and provide additional after-school and holiday provision, including a cooked meal and a variety of engaging activities.
Clubs
Our extracurricular clubs are thoughtfully designed for younger children, offering a wide range of inclusive activities delivered both by our school team and trusted external providers. Reception children are invited to join clubs from the Spring term, allowing them time to settle confidently into school life first.
Extra Curricular Activities
Trips
Our trips are designed to bring learning to life through hands-on, immersive experiences they help to deepen understanding in an engaging and memorable way.
School Admissions
If you would like to speak to our Early Years Lead or the Trust Admissions Officer Lisa Tilleray, please click here to complete an enquiry form. The relevant member of staff will contact you as soon as they can.
For general enquiries about the school, please contact the school office on 020 8647 9322 or by e-mail to office@stanleyparkinfants.co.uk.
Transfer to Stanley Park Juniors School
If you are offered and accept a place at Stanley Park Infant's School your child will transfer to the Junior School for Year 3 to Year 6 providing a Junior school application is completed. For further information about the junior school, please click here to view their website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wrap Around Care - Stanley Park Infants' School
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
School Led Breakfast Club - Busy Bees
The school has a commitment to providing excellent wrap around care with facilities that support both parents and children's needs.
We offer a selection of cereals and fresh milk. Toast with a variety of spreads - sweet and savoury, fresh fruit and yoghurt. Children are offered drinks of pure juice, water, milk or hot chocolate in the winter months. Breakfast is eaten in a relaxed, informal atmosphere with music and conversation. Children are then free to play with toys, puzzles, colouring or reading.
The Breakfast Club operates during term time only and is staffed by members of the whole school team. The team are trained in Child Care, Food Hygiene and First Aid.
Breakfast Club has up to forty places and operates Monday-Friday - 7.45 - 8.45 am.
Children are then escorted by staff to their classes to begin their school day.
Children must be pre-registered for the Breakfast Club and there is a daily fee of £5.00 per child per session. It is important that children are booked into the Breakfast Club and that payment is made in advance via Parent Pay.
Children can also be booked in on an ad-hoc basis for a one off day or more rather than committing to regular attendance. Again, children must be registered and payment made in advance. The fee for this option is £6.50 per child per session.
Further details and registration forms can be obtained from the school office.
The Aims of the Breakfast Club are:
We accept payments via Childcare vouchers, the school's Ofsted reference number is 145385
Breakfast Club Information and Application Form
School Led Afterschool Club - Bumbles
The school has a commitment to providing excellent wrap around care with facilities that support both parents and children's needs. In September 2022 the school opened a school-led after school provision to meet the needs of the school community.
Bumbles has up to 30 places starting straight from school until 5.00pm during term time. Bumbles is not open on INSET days or early finish times on the last day of a school term.
We offer a snack of fruit and a biscuit (not chocolate), accompanied by a drink of milk, fruit juice, or water.
We provide a variety of play activities – jigsaws, construction, art, playdough, role play, board games, floor games etc. The activities are varied each day in order that all the children can enjoy a varied spectrum of play. All staff are qualified or experienced in either Childcare or Playwork and First Aid.
Children must be pre-registered for Bumbles; there is a daily fee of £8.50 per child per session or £11.00 per child per session for ad-hoc sessions. It is important that children are booked to attend and that payment is made in advance via Parent Pay. We accept payments via Childcare vouchers, the school's Ofsted reference number is 145385
Further details and registration forms can be obtained from the school office.
The Aims of Bumbles are:
Bumbles Information Pack and Application Form
Jancett Afterschool and Holiday Club
Stanleys After School Club and Holiday Club
Stanleys is run for Stanley Park Infants and Junior Schools by Jancett Group of Day Nurseries in the Infants School Hall. Our partnership with Jancett has been running since 2005 and in that time the club has received a 'good' inspection with outstanding features from OFSTED.
After School Club runs every school day from 3.15p.m - 6.30p.m and is supervised by at least four fully qualified workers with a club manager overseeing activities. The children are given a snack tea and take part in a range of indoor and outdoor activities.
For more information on Stanleys After School Club or Holiday Club please contact:

16 Stanley Park Road
